newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah weakens on ample liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah weakens on ample liquidity.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah weakened against the dollar in moderate early trading on Wednesday on the back of excess supply, dealers said.
They said the market was mainly liquidity-driven, but small increases of short-dated swaps had made operators alert.
"Ample supply has caused the rupiah to weaken in the morning. But offshore buying is limiting further declines," one said.
"The underlying tone seems to be biddish on dollars, but offshore selling orders placed at the 2,389 and 2,390 levels have capped the upside," the foreign bank dealer said.
Spot rupiah fell to 2,388.30/88.65 at 0330 GMT from 2,385.75/86.75 at the opening. Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,388.0/88.5 and 2,388.00/88.35, respectively.

Overnight swaps edged down to 0.10/0.15 from 0.15/0.25. But tom/next and spot/next swaps inched up slightly to 0.25/0.35 and 0.90/1.00, respectively, on worries of a possible tightening because of anticipated higher tax payments.
One U.S. bank dealer said swaps were also driven down on ample rupiah supply, but some rises in tom/next and spot/next woke the market and triggered a rebound in swaps.
One-month swaps were at 11.0/11.5, two at 24.0/25.5, three at 37.0/39.0 and six at 76.5/77.5 points.
One local bank dealer said short-term swaps remained volatile while longer-term rates were rather stable.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,379/2,571 and the conversion band also by one point to 2,379/2,427 on Tuesday, the first in the week.
The bank depreciated the rupiah by two points last week after lowering it by four points the previous week.
